_comment: Lived-experience excerpts. SHORT verbatim quotations with attribution, used as grounding for teacher generation only. The full articles are copyrighted and are NOT vendored. Entries are licence 'all-rights-reserved', so they are NOT trainable text: the pipeline must use them to inform teacher-written replies, never as training targets. See ../LICENSES.md.

accounts.author: dylan
accounts.title: My brain is a browser with 400 tabs open and somehow I built a business out of the one that was
accounts.excerpt: I would get hired somewhere, be incredible for six months, and then slowly unravel as the novelty wore off and the executive dysfunction kicked in. Not because I was lazy. Not because I didn't care. Because my brain literally could not maintain interest in something that had become routine.
accounts.use: situation vocabulary; teaches that 'unmotivated' must never be echoed back

accounts.author: dylan
accounts.title: My brain is a browser with 400 tabs open (2)
accounts.excerpt: For my entire adult life, I have experienced work as a thing I do despite my brain. A constant negotiation between what needs to happen and what my neurochemistry will allow.
accounts.use: situations about forcing a routine task after the spark has gone

accounts.author: dylan
accounts.title: My brain is a browser with 400 tabs open (3)
accounts.excerpt: I still have days where I can't focus on anything and days where I focus on the wrong thing for nine hours.
accounts.use: situations about fluctuating capacity; the coach must not treat a bad day as failure

accounts.author: Carmen Irace
accounts.title: AuDHD + Executive Dysfunction: Why You Know What to Do... and Still Can't Do It
accounts.excerpt: If you are AuDHD, executive dysfunction can feel like living with a beautiful brain... and a cursed "Start" button.
accounts.use: situation vocabulary for the knowing-but-cannot-start pattern

accounts.author: Carmen Irace
accounts.title: AuDHD + Executive Dysfunction (2)
accounts.excerpt: EFs are 'united but separable.' You can be solid at one (say, creativity and quick thinking) and still face-plant at another (task initiation or transitions).
accounts.use: teaches the coach not to infer capability from one strong domain

accounts.author: Carmen Irace
accounts.title: AuDHD + Executive Dysfunction (3)
accounts.excerpt: Why do planners work for two weeks and then die? Because many planners demand consistent initiation, consistent review, and consistent time awareness - three things executive dysfunction makes inconsistent.
themes: systems that fail at week two
accounts.use: situations about abandoning a system; the coach suggests restarting, not abandoning

accounts.author: Rebekah & Co.
accounts.title: Dear Boss, It's Not Laziness - It's Executive Dysfunction (A Love Letter from My AuDHD Brain)
accounts.excerpt: You set an alarm for a meeting, then immediately forget why the alarm is going off. Every. Time.
accounts.use: situation vocabulary; the app's timer and journal exist precisely for this

accounts.author: Rebekah & Co.
accounts.title: Dear Boss, It's Not Laziness (2)
accounts.excerpt: You spend 3 hours hyper-fixating on redesigning your entire planner to make it perfect ... and then forget to actually do any of the tasks in said planner.
accounts.use: situations about building a system instead of doing the work

accounts.author: Rebekah & Co.
accounts.title: Dear Boss, It's Not Laziness (3)
accounts.excerpt: It's not a matter of willpower. It's a matter of support, understanding, and occasionally, noise-canceling headphones and crying in your car on your lunch break.
accounts.use: explicitly forbids the willpower/shame register in replies

accounts.author: ScienceWorks Behavioral Healthcare (clinician review: Dr. Kiesa Kelly)
accounts.title: Executive Dysfunction in Adults: Why You Can't Start
accounts.excerpt: Executive dysfunction is a 'how the system runs' issue, not a 'how much you care' issue.
accounts.use: the core validation sentence, clinically reviewed; a licence-free paraphrase of this idea belongs in replies

accounts.author: ScienceWorks Behavioral Healthcare
accounts.title: Executive Dysfunction in Adults: Why You Can't Start (2)
accounts.excerpt: Losing steps mid-task because working memory gets overloaded. Underestimating time and transitions, sometimes called time blindness.
